title: Inside Toyota's Hybrid Inverter-Converter Assembly: MGECU, IPM, and High-Voltage Powertrain

locations.name: Under the hood, driver's side of the engine bay (explicitly mentioned; Prius 3rd generation)
locations.basis: Transcript line: 'under the hood on the driver's side of the engine bay you will have one of these' and reference to a 'third generation Prius'.

summary: This video provides a meticulous, hands-on exploration of Toyota’s inverter-converter assembly—the 'brain' of the hybrid system. The host identifies key components (MG ECU, Intelligent Power Modules, DC-DC converter, boost converter), explains how high-voltage DC from the battery is turned into three-phase AC for MG1 and MG2, and covers cooling, thermal management, and sensor networks. The segment includes a close look at a failed IPM, discussion of safety features, and practical repair considerations, including cost and labor implications of replacing versus repairing the inverter. Historical context is provided by comparing to early Prius designs, highlighting how hybrid power electronics have evolved over time.
topics: Three-phase AC motors MG1 and MG2
Atmospheric pressure sensor in circuit board
MG1 charging MG2 and starting engine
AC versus DC power and three-phase wiring
Common IPM failure modes and heat damage
Labor and cost economics of inverter repair vs replacement
Capacitors and energy storage in the boost circuit
System diagnostics and Toyota trouble codes

featured_techniques.technique: Live inspection of a failed IPM shows burnt IGBTs and degraded thermal paste, illustrating heat damage and cooling failure.
Demonstration of DC-DC and boost converter operation, including the coil energization and capacitor energy storage to reach ~650V.
Discussion of safety features and insulation testing (mega-ohm meter), including high-voltage wiring insulation containment.
Case opening with a specialized tool and emphasis on precise torque, sealing, and thermal interface materials for rebuilds.
